title: How we check synthetic NPC voices when players are learning the language by ear
author: Square-Taro-9122
selftext:
I’m Jonathan, the developer of WonderLang. In the sequel there’s a Korean-speaking otter. For the trailer I auditioned four synthetic voices for its line, and none sounded like the character. It took a second set to find one I wanted to use.



Casting and language review are separate jobs for us. In WonderLang Beyond the dialogue is written ahead of time. We generate recordings for those lines, and native speakers check them. A learner might listen to a sentence several times to work out what a character means, so getting the words and pronunciation right matters as much as finding a voice that suits an otter.



For anyone else voicing a multilingual cast, do you have your reviewers listen to each line on its own or play through the whole conversation first? I’d be interested in what you catch one way that you miss the other.



The trailer with the otter is on our Kickstarter: [https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/jonathan-wonderlang/wonderlang-beyond-a-language-learning-rpg-for-intermediates](https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/jonathan-wonderlang/wonderlang-beyond-a-language-learning-rpg-for-intermediates)
